questions.label: Water availability
questions.prompt: Is the water available to land and plants changing?

variables.why: Rain is the input of the land water balance.
Root-zone soil moisture represents estimated water stored in the soil available to plants.
The top 10 cm respond fastest to rain and drying.
Evapotranspiration is the water returned to the air; where water is scarce it follows rain.
Vegetation would show the biological response — not processed yet.
River flow would show the hydrological response — not processed yet.

questions.label: Coastal climate
questions.prompt: Do the coast and the interior of a region behave the same?

variables.why: Air temperature of each native cell, classified as coastal or interior in QGIS.
A second reanalysis at the same points.
A coastal weather station.
Sea-surface temperature would add the ocean side — planned.

questions.label: Andean snow
questions.prompt: How do snow and temperature vary together?

variables.why: Warm years may melt or prevent snow.
Water stored in the snowpack (model).
Snow needs precipitation too.

ERA5, another reanalysis.
Punta Arenas station.

variables.why: Pre-registered main variable.

questions.label: Vegetation response
questions.prompt: How does vegetation respond to environmental change?

variables.why: Satellite greenness — available at NASA but not processed in this version.
Modelled evapotranspiration is the closest integrated proxy.
Water available to roots.

questions.unavailable: No vegetation index is integrated yet: MOD13C2 has no subsetting service we could use and AppEEARS needs a user login. Closest available alternative: evapotranspiration and soil moisture (GLDAS model).

cards.title: Antofagasta warmed faster than Los Lagos (MERRA-2)

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27); test on the difference series
analysis.correction: nominal p applies (planned comparison); q across 120 pairs shown

checks.dependency: one point; may be assimilated by reanalyses

cards.title: Antofagasta's coast did not warm; its interior did

source.product: MERRA-2; cells classified in QGIS; CIREN DEM for cell elevations

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27); difference series

thresholds.rule: centre within 30 km of the coast

checks.source: ERA5 at 4 coastal and 5 interior cell centres

checks.dependency: one point; may be assimilated by reanalyses

cards.can: The regional mean hides a coast–interior contrast present in two reanalyses and consistent with the coastal station.
cards.cannot: It does not establish the cause; coast and elevation are strongly correlated (ρ = 0.90) and the elevation-range-restricted comparison is not exact matching.
open: Role of the cool coastal ocean (SST not yet integrated)
Falvey & Garreaud (2009) found a related contrast for 1979–2006
limitations: coastal cells mix ocean and land
exploratory, decided after seeing the regional result

cards.title: Rain and root-zone soil moisture move together in central Chile
cards.variable: IMERG precipitation vs GLDAS root-zone soil moisture

analysis.method: Pearson r of detrended yearly anomalies; effective sample size (Bretherton et al. 1999)

cards.can: Year-to-year, wetter years have wetter soils in this region.
cards.cannot: GLDAS is driven by observed precipitation, so the agreement is partly built in; it is not independent evidence or a cause.
open: River discharge (CAMELS-CL) and vegetation (MODIS) would add independent responses

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27)

cards.can: Precipitation trends over ~25 years depend strongly on where the record starts.
